attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post. The tweets and the I. J. Good quote set up the context. They are not the claim.

semantics.note: Marcus calls the idea that AI has reached a beyond-AGI, Good-style level 'laughable'. That is a firm present-tense denial. The normalised claim keeps both that standard and the scope (current AI).

contract.note: On the plain reading, the standard is reliable breadth across intellectual tasks, judged on July 2026 capabilities. That is an ordinary, fair reading of his words. 'Laughable' is treated as emphasis, and the separate count of Marcus–Brundage tasks is rightly left out.

evidence.note: ARC Prize post dated July 6, 2026, inside the target period. It says the novel interactive tasks are easy for humans but still hard for current AI. That is an independent benchmark showing a gap against human performance.

ARC Prize result dated July 24, 2026. The best model scored 30.2% on ARC-AGI-3, and many environments were near zero. Its high ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 scores show strength in narrower areas, not superiority across everything.

reviews.rationale: Independent July 2026 benchmark results show leading AI still far behind humans on novel interactive reasoning tasks that humans find easy. That meets the support condition. Strong scores on older benchmarks do not show reliable expert-level ability across all intellectual work, so the contradiction condition is not met.
